children: Automobile heavyweights Eicher Motors and Hero MotoCorp shares fell up to 6 per cent on Wednesday amid selling pressure driven by a combination of macroeconomic and industry-wide factors.

“Even though domestic demand remains resilient, a sharp drop in export dispatches and modest channel-filling ahead of the festive season triggered a classic profit-taking reaction following recent multi-month rallies,” said Mayank Jain, Market Analyst, Share.Market by PhonePe.

The selling pressure across automobile stocks also came as broader market sentiment turned cautious due to rising global crude oil prices, which directly increase fuel running costs and freight expenses across the automotive supply chain.
At the same time, ongoing supply chain and logistics frictions have created localised delivery bottlenecks. This macro weakness coincided with the release of August volume dispatches, Jain said.
Eicher Motors witnessed a sharp single-day pullback, falling nearly 4 per cent to trade around the 7,654 level after facing strong technical resistance near the psychological 8,200 mark.
The stock has broken below its short-term 20-day moving average (20 MA) at 8,008.1 and is currently testing its intermediate 50-day moving average at 7,740.2 as immediate support.
A sustained move below this zone could open room towards its primary 200-day moving average at 7,365.7, which remains the key structural support.

As the stock's broader long-term trajectory over the past year remains positive, technical indicators point to a higher probability of price consolidation within the 7,365-7,740 range rather than an immediate trend reversal.

Market participants are likely to adopt a wait-and-watch approach to assess whether buying interest emerges near these major moving average support levels before expecting a possible resumption of upward momentum.
Hero MotoCorp witnessed notable selling pressure, declining over 5 per cent to 5,255 after facing strong resistance near the 6,000 zone.
The recent decline pushed the stock below both its short-term 20-day moving average at 5,676.3 and its key long-term 200-day moving average at 5,419.0.
The price is now hovering near its intermediate 50-day moving average at 5,293.7.

A move below the 200-day moving average reflects heightened short-term volatility and active distribution. Given that the stock recently formed a lower peak compared with its late-2025 highs, the probability currently favours a period of sideways, range-bound movement between the 5,000 support level and the 5,500 resistance zone.
Investors will likely monitor whether the 4,800-5,000 support band holds to assess if price stability could precede any renewed upward move.
